correctness.rationale: Full constructive upper bound follows from an exact factorization, and the lower bound exhausts all signed base-power representatives below k0. The 2B-b^j branch is rigorously above k0; the remaining branches are excluded modulo b^c+1 using 2c|d and oddness. No infinite claim depends on finite enumeration. A separate modular-inverse residue enumeration confirms 300 parameter triples.

originality.rationale: Three full arXiv primary manuscripts and the later sharp single-factor theorem were checked at their relevant definitions, statements and Fermat-factor arguments. Their hypotheses and conclusions do not imply an exact minimal coefficient under two fixed coprime plus-one divisibility conditions. Multiple published-finding corpus semantic queries and literal web searches found no stronger/equivalent statement. This is best-knowledge originality, not exhaustive priority certification.
residual_risks: An older cyclotomic congruence/CRT article or an unindexed Fermat-number note may contain an equivalent minimal coefficient formulation.
Semantic-index snippets do not establish noncoverage of every repository item; only near hits and accessible primary full texts were compared.
The theorem is elementary, and parallel discovery outside indexed literature cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: The minimal coefficient for two prescribed generalized Fermat divisors is a natural sharp arithmetic obstruction in exponential Carmichael-candidate investigations. One-factor prime bounds cannot resolve the simultaneous existence threshold, and the exact formula covers an infinite, structurally characterized family of mutually coprime plus-one moduli with no primality assumptions. This provides an actionable exclusion for all smaller coefficients and an explicit sharp witness, not a routine restatement of a known one-factor inequality.
